what: CREATURE LANGUAGE PACK (build L1, 2026-10-21): the words for the parts of an animal or a fantasy creature (a dragon: claws, horns, teeth, eyes, wings, tail, legs) and how they are recognised from the measured descriptors of the parts engine/tools/language.py segments. Data only; over engine/packs/generic/language.json. The rules are tried in order; a rule names only parts not named yet, so the specific words come first and the generic ones (engine/packs/generic) last.

vocabulary.body: the core mass (trunk) the other parts grow from
vocabulary.head: the protrusion at the front that carries the most points (horns, teeth, jaws, whiskers)
vocabulary.leg: a limb that carries claws (fore or hind by where it grows from)
vocabulary.claw: a short pointed tip at the end of a limb
vocabulary.horn: a pointed protrusion of the head, or high on the front of the body
vocabulary.tooth: a small pointed tip at the front of the head, low (in the mouth)
vocabulary.tongue: the front-most protrusion, low and forward
vocabulary.tail: the longest slender protrusion behind the body
vocabulary.spike: a pointed protrusion along the back or the tail (dorsal spines, the points of a heraldic wing)
vocabulary.wing: a thin wide plate high on the body
vocabulary.eye: a small closed separate shell high at the front

sources.what: the words are plain English anatomy and heraldry (claw, horn, tail, wing, spike, tongue)

segmentation.why: a creature is a body with protrusions; eyes and teeth are often separate shells in a modelled creature

branches.why: a 3-D creature carries small points (claws, teeth, spines) a few mm long on a body some cm thick: tips that outlive their merge by 0.08 core radii, parts down to 0.02 % of the surface (cases/dragon3d, build L1); a drawing keeps the generic values (0.08 cut the heraldic dragon's tail and hind leg into notches, cases/dragon2d)

frame: 3-D: up = +z, front = -y (the job's up / front turn the model so); 2-D: up = +y, front = the way the creature faces (the job's front, +x or -x)

findings._: measured findings (build L1, 2026-10-21): what was done, what resulted, where; evidence, not rules

items.what: Planted creature: every point found and named
items.result: Smooth union of an ellipsoid body, 4 legs x 3 claws, a head with 2 horns and a tapering tail (marching cubes 1.5 mm): claws 12 of 12 at IoU 0.82-0.92 named claw (foreleg_L_claw_2 ...), horns 0.92-0.93, tail 0.88, legs 0.77-0.84 named foreleg / hindleg L / R. A drawn 2-D creature: 4 legs and 8 claws found and named.

31 parts, 29 named: 4 legs with 16 claws, horns, spikes (the wing's points), tongue, tail (its arrow tip); the wing and head stay in the body (59 % of the area: no flare separates them in a silhouette). A re-rendering at 1280 px moved no address over 0.032 mm (p99); a horn erased: reported gone, the rest p99 <= 0.081 mm.
items.status: checked (object.png read by eye; change tests)

items.result: 17 parts, 16 named (horns, spikes, feet, tongue, tail fin, one claw); the body holds 88.5 % of the surface: no flare separates the head, neck, legs or the coiled tail from it, and the body's tube chart addresses 19.6 % of its vertices (the rest xyz). Between the scan's 100k- and 437k-vertex reconstructions (surfaces 0.09 mm apart at p50, 0.28 mm p99) the median part moved 0.08 mm, but 542 of 4,255 addresses moved over 1 mm (worst part p99 9.5 mm, on the feet) and 337 missed.
items.status: checked; big-part segmentation and thin scanned parts OPEN

items.what: Taper is measured along the part, not along its chord
items.result: On the heraldic dragon the chord-based taper of curved claws read 0.7-2.2 (none passed as pointed); the ring radius along the walking distance from the tip (tip third / base third) read 0.19-0.47 for claws and about 1 for legs.
